# Keys you hand over - qa-doc-scribe

## Outputs

- `test-report.md` - the scribe writes it; --close-gate-b appends the decision

Required at your stop (stage S8): `work/ledger.json`, `work/ledger.md`, `test-report.md`.
Re-run by the gate at your stop: `check_coverage.py`.

## Witness

Your witness artifact (stages.json `witness`): `test-report.md`.

## Handoff form

Contract `s8-scribe-to-gate-b` (fill `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml`; `handoff_check.py` reads it):

- `inputs_read[].version` (required) - its window id
- `inputs_read[].drafts_received` (required) - n
- `inputs_read[].rows` (required) - n
- `header.window` (required) - TICKET
- `header.verdict` (required) - one of vocabulary.header_verdicts
- `stage_acceptance.failure_class` (required) - spec|capability|data|tooling
- `stage_acceptance.quote` (required) - the analyst's own words, with path#anchor
- `stage_acceptance.witness_paths[]` (optional) - task-relative path the verdict rests on, or omit when none
- `delivery.ready` (required) - yes|after_checks|no
- `delivery.blocked_by` (required) - the ledger's own list; exactly ['factory'] is said in the first sentence
- `questions[].id` (required) - gap or bug or delivery item
- `questions[].question` (required) - as the section words it
- `questions[].answers` (required) - the closed set - e.g. fix now | verify elsewhere | defer with a reminder | accept
- `rehearsal.ran` (required) - true|false
- `rehearsal.factory_fixable_open` (required) - n
- `rehearsal.person_decides` (required) - the findings that became questions above
- `rehearsal.factory_defect` (required) - stated plainly, in the words its fix prints; the person's word that passes it is recorded by the conductor
- `claims.every_section_is_quoted_from_the_command_named` (required) - true|false
- `claims.no_factory_owned_reason_is_put_to_the_person_as_a_choice` (required) - true|false
- `claims.no_gate_a_decision_is_asked_again` (required) - true|false
- `claims.the_bug_list_is_built_by_code_and_numbered` (required) - true|false
- `claims.traceability_table_exists_on_disk` (required) - true|false
- `claims.s8_was_closed_before_the_gate_was_asked` (required) - true|false
- `tried[].requirement` (required) - the claim of the report, in a few words
- `tried[].technique` (required) - the code block or tool output the claim rests on
- `tried[].observation` (required) - what it shows, in one line
- `tried[].evidence` (required) - the path (and anchor) where it shows
- `tried_note` (optional) - why the table is empty, or a dash when it has rows
- `unresolved[].id` (required) - row or item
- `unresolved[].reason` (required) - one of vocabulary.unresolved_reasons
- `unresolved[].detail` (required) - what exactly is missing, and what would settle it
- `blocked.field` (only when blocked) - the field of this file the role cannot fill
- `blocked.problem` (only when blocked) - what the role tried and what refused it, verbatim
- `blocked.tried[]` (only when blocked) - command or step, and its answer
- `blocked.data[]` (only when blocked) - path of anything the conductor needs to see

Every handoff form shares one skeleton (`common_shape` of handoffs/index.yaml): `inputs`, `inputs_read`, `header`, `scope`, `artifacts`, `claims`, `unresolved`, `blocked`.

## What code will check of you

`<T>` is your ticket, `<ID>` your dispatch id, `<home>` the project's qa-factory folder - all three stand in your prompt (`Ticket: ... Dispatch: ...`) and in your task packet.

- [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] Your final message is the handoff form: a header `<role> <stage> <window> · ok|concerns|halt|impossible`; one line `<id> · <state> · <reason of at most 80 characters>` for every item of the dispatch's scope (a halting digest owes no scope lines); nothing but those lines between the header and the path; and, last, the task-relative path of what you wrote (a halting digest may omit it). A verdict or a state word outside the form's list is advice, not a refusal; a reason over 80 characters, an absolute path under the task root, prose before the header and a missing path the witness names are mended by code when mending makes the form pass. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [exit_gate:EG-text-end] Your dispatch ends with the host's handback tool carrying your digest line, never with free text after it. Door: call the host's handback tool with your digest line.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-artifact-rewrite] An artifact that exists with content, and whose `artifact-writers.json` entry carries `rewrite`, is never replaced whole by Write. Door: the point edit the entry's `rewrite` names (quoted in the refusal).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-big-read] A file over `config.read.max_bytes` is read with `offset`/`limit`, a PDF with a `pages` range within `config.read.max_pdf_pages`, and a picture only up to `config.read.max_image_bytes`. Door: `Grep -n` for the line, then Read with `offset`/`limit`; a PDF by `pages` ranges.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-case-store] When the project declares `cases_root`, a case file is written inside it and nowhere else. Door: write it as `<cases_root>/<area>/<case id>.md`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-command-size] A Bash or PowerShell command is at most 64 KB (65,536 characters); a longer one is refused before any other check reads it. Door: split the work into several commands, or write the long text to a file with Write and name the file.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-config-write] A role never writes `qa-factory/config.json`, by Write, Edit, NotebookEdit or a shell write shape. Door: name `launch: <cause>` (or `launch: unknown`) and the evidence line in your digest.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-direct-test-run] Tests are never launched directly (any form of `launch-causes.json` `run_forms`): outside a dispatch through `run_suite.py --task <T> --label <label> -- <command>`, inside an open dispatch only through a typed request; a command that runs no test carries its runner's no-run flag. Door: `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>` (inside a dispatch); `run_suite.py --template request` prints a request skeleton.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-external-writes] No shell command writes to a tracker or a test-management system (a declared `external_writes` command, a tracker CLI with a write verb and object, or an `api` call with a write method). Door: write a proposal file under `work/proposals/` in the shape `external-writes.md` defines.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-git-config] A shell command never changes git configuration: `git config` passes only with `--get`, `--get-all`, `--get-regexp`, `--get-urlmatch`, `--list` or `-l`. Door: report the blocker in your digest; the person decides.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-code-file] `<ID>.values.applied.yaml` and `<ID>.values.stale.yaml` are written by code only. Door: write your fields to `<ID>.values.yaml`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-edit-pending] A handover form is not edited while its `<ID>.values.yaml` waits to be applied. Door: put the field into `<ID>.values.yaml` (rewrite it whole with the field added).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-rewrite] A handover form that exists is never rewritten whole by Write. Door: Write `work/handoffs/<ID>.values.yaml` with `path: value` lines, or Edit one field.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-values] A Write of `<ID>.values.yaml` lands only when the form with those values merged is ready (every word from its list, every line parses, every path known), or when it fills `blocked.problem`. Door: rewrite the file with the kept lines and the fixed lines the refusal lists; what you cannot fill goes to `blocked.field` and `blocked.problem`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-human-word] A role never runs a command that records a person's word: `waiver.py --stage` or `--carry-from`, `ticket_adapter.py accept-gap` or `review --record`, `source_exclusions.py --load` or `--revoke`, `stand_identity.py record|confirm|forget|unconfirm`, `environment_record.py record|revoke`, `project_knowledge.py account|role|revoke|side|lesson`, `report_adapt.py kind|forget`, `story_step.py decide`. Door: return the open point in your digest.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-logs] An evidence `.log` or `.junit.xml` heavier than `guards.raw_log_free_bytes` (default 8192 bytes) is never read whole, by Read or by a shell command (a command that mentions `run_suite` is exempt). Door: read the `<label>-<ts>.json` summary beside the log (`error_head`, failed names); with a shell, `run_suite.py --request <file> --detail <test>`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-owner] An artifact owned by a role is written only by that role, or while a dispatch of that role is open for the story. Door: name it in your digest; the conductor sends it back to its owner (`controller.py --operation rework`).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-patch-unchecked] A write whose content the guard can read; a patch it cannot parse is blocked. Door: a patch in the host's grammar (`*** Begin Patch` / `*** End Patch`, a path per section).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-plugin-read] A role's Read, Grep or Glob never targets the installed plugin outside its `references/` folder. Door: read your brief `work/briefs/<ID>.md` and the plugin's `references/`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-stand-record-write] A role never writes `records/stand-identity.json`, `records/environment-properties.json`, `records/report-adaptations.json`, `records/project-knowledge.json` or a story's `state/stand-confirmations.jsonl`. Door: hand off as a halt with the row `stand · blocked · <what>` and the evidence line in `blocked`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-unparsed-event] (No requirement the role can meet: the host's hook event could not be read.). Door: try the call once more; the second time the factory records a finding and the conductor is called.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-walker-error] A shell command is one the guard's command reader can walk. Door: several simpler commands, or the long text written to a file with Write.
- [handoff_check:blocked_problem] A row in state `blocked` carries `blocked.problem`; `blocked_by_env` is used only where `options_for_role` offers it to this role. Door: write the problem, or pick a state the role is offered.
- [handoff_check:claims] What the form claims is true is true on disk ("the form claims this is true, and it is not"). Door: fix the claim or make it true.
- [handoff_check:cli] The call names an existing UTF-8 form with a `contract:` line and an existing values file; `--shorten` only with `--fix`. Door: the refusal's door; a non-UTF-8 form: run `handoff_init` again (:3040-3041).
- [handoff_check:field.blank] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page) Door: write the value as a `path: value` line in the values file, then run the check again.
- [handoff_check:field.max_len] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page) Door: shorten it (`--shorten` with `--fix`) or rewrite.
- [handoff_check:field.value] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page) Door: write one of the listed words (or `new: <word> -- <why>` where the list is open).
- [handoff_check:findings_tooling] A finding whose cause is `tooling` is repeated in `tooling_findings`. Door: add it to `tooling_findings`.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.failures] Each shown failure has a triage row. Door: triage it once.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.listing] Everything named in `listed_in` exists, and nothing extra stands. Door: list exactly what exists.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.names] Every row has a name. Door: name the row.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.repairs] No repair is pending when the null outcome is claimed. Door: finish or record the repair.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.report] The run report is readable. Door: rerun / point at the readable report.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.verdict] The triage verdict is a known word. Door: write a known verdict.
- [handoff_check:required_rows] A required list has one row per item in scope: the id, a state and a reason of at most 80 characters. Door: write the rows as index lines in the values file, then run this check again.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.null_word] A list's null-outcome word (the declared empty outcome) stands only when the list has no rows; never both. Door: remove the word or remove the rows.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.owed_by_verdict] When the verdict owes rows (the verdict word names work done on items), the list is not empty. Door: write the rows the verdict owes, or change the verdict.
- [handoff_check:tried] In a contract that asks what was tried (TRIED_CONTRACTS), each tried entry states what was tried and the error it gave (TRIED_MEANING). Door: fill the tried entry with the attempt and its error.
- [handoff_check:values_apply] Each path names a field of this contract, by its index where it is a list row, not a contract-owned path; a list field gets a list and a one-value field one value; rows open in order. Door: correct the path (the refusal suggests "did you mean").
- [handoff_check:values_file] The values file is `path: value` lines (or a JSON object): valid JSON, an object not a list, each path given once, each key a field path, no nested value. Door: fix the line the refusal names (FILE_FIX).
- [host_adapter:HA-call-shape] A tool call has a shape the host adapter can read (a command as text or an argv list, one call per code cell, no tty option). Door: send the command as text or as an argv list.
- [host_adapter:HA-connector-orchestrator] A caller with a shell never calls a connector tool that `host_tools.read_only` does not list. Door: name it in your digest; the conductor registers a verified read-only tool.
- [host_adapter:HA-exec-tty] On Codex, an `exec_command` call never asks for a tty. Door: a non-interactive call.
- [host_adapter:HA-no-command-text] On Codex, every command call carries its command text (the field words of FIELD_WORDS; in a code cell, the literal `tools.exec_command({cmd: ...})`). Door: send the command in the fields the refusal names.
- [host_adapter:HA-role-nested-delegation] On Codex, a role with its own agent file does not delegate to another agent. Door: name the need in your digest; the conductor dispatches.
- [host_adapter:HA-stdin-chars] On Codex, a `write_stdin` call never sends characters to a running process. Door: a guarded `exec_command` call.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.commit.manifest] A commit does not leave a manifest case unresolved without a reason from the closed vocabulary (`closed_unresolved_reasons()` or `deferred:<gate>`). Door: write the reason on the case.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.commit.pathspec] A commit names its paths (or uses `--`) and never `-a` or `--all`. Door: git commit -m "..." -- <paths>.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.delivery] Before gate B, a delivery form is written only when the ledger word is `yes` or `after_checks`, or a deliver_with_risks journal line stands. Door: write it without those words, split it, or file it.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.opaque] Inside an open dispatch, a command that launches the runner holds none of the forms the shell reads differently from the guard (`hooklib.SHELL_OPAQUE_BAN`, e.g. a backslash-escaped quote). Door: write it without that form, or launch `run_suite.py --request FILE` as its own command.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.request] The `--request` file exists (or the same command writes it), parses, and each request names the running dispatch's `dispatch_id` and selects only instances inside its scope (an instance is in scope when the manifest says it `covers` a scope case). Door: `run_suite.py --template request`; add the case to `covers` through `manifest_put.py`.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.stash] A `git stash` names its paths. Door: name the paths.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.typed_runner] Inside an open dispatch, tests run only through `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`, `--request FILE` or `--schedule FILE`, with the runner's path and flags written literally (no `$(...)`, backtick pair or `(Join-Path ...)`); `--task/--label` and the default full suite are refused. Door: `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`.
- [stage_guard:SG-walker-error] A shell command is one the stage guard's command reader can walk. Door: several simpler commands, or the long text written to a file.
- [exit_gate:digest] Your final message is the handoff form: a header `<role> <stage> <window> · ok|concerns|halt|impossible`; one line `<id> · <state> · <reason of at most 80 characters>` for every item of the dispatch's scope (a halting digest owes no scope lines); nothing but those lines between the header and the path; and, last, the task-relative path of what you wrote (a halting digest may omit it). A verdict or a state word outside the form's list is advice, not a refusal; a reason over 80 characters, an absolute path under the task root, prose before the header and a missing path the witness names are mended by code when mending makes the form pass. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [validate_artifacts:check_legacy_report_sections] (legacy form) Every gate-B section stands, in order. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_ptr_readiness] `Readiness within what was verified` gives every register requirement a row with a status from its list. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_blocks] Every code-owned block stands with its markers, opens with its own heading and holds no section heading; "Decided at gate B" stands only when gate B has recorded words, and never quotes gate A's. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_coverage] The report's coverage line enumerates the check coverage. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_forbidden] The report carries none of the factory's internal identifiers, and no decision marker without its decision text. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_gate_b] "Decided at gate B" quotes the person's recorded words for each decision, never a paraphrase. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_human_text] Each `Factory defects` item is written in plain words, as `human-questions.md` asks. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_ledger_and_readiness] Hand text outside the generated tables stays within `TEST_REPORT_MAX_BYTES`, section 1 is the table `ledger.py` generated, and a `delivery_ready: yes|after_checks|no` line agrees with `ledger.json`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_left_with_you] Every `Left with you` item names its requirement and case, what a person would observe, and how. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_sections] Every template section stands, in the template's order, with the verdict and its `delivery_ready:` line above the rest. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_test_marks] Every test line under `Proven`, and every test a `Left with you` item names, carries the real-or-mock mark the ledger records. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_report_traceability] Every register requirement and every plan case stands in a row of the traceability appendix. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_test_report] `work/delivery-summary.md` is readable and fresh (regenerated when stale). Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.

### Not yet in rows

test-report.md is read by code, not skimmed. Begin it from the template and run `report_facts.py --task <T> --write`: it renders the code-owned blocks (the verdict, Proven, Product bugs, Open questions, Skipped by the plan, Not proven, Decided at gate A, Size, Where to look; Decided at gate B after the gate) and you never type a number they carry. The `delivery_ready:` line is the block's (check_delivery.py feeds it): yes, after_checks or no. Eleven sections in this order: Proven, Product bugs, Left with you, Open questions, Not proven, Decided at gate A, Decided at gate B, Factory defects, Size, Where to look, Appendix - the verdict above the first. A green test the critic could not verify is in Left with you, not under Proven. Left with you has one item per case in `ledger.json` `left_items`, each with its R-n, case id, `To check:` and `Needed:` or `How:`; its last two blocks are code's. The Appendix is `traceability.py --render` pasted, a row for every R and every case. `report_facts.py --task <T> --check` must exit 0 before you finish. Your prose outside the blocks stays under 6,144 bytes. check_coverage.py re-runs at the exit gate: regenerate the coverage map first.
